parole.testo: From أَب (ʔab) and هَوْل (hawl): “the dreadful one,” literally “father of dread.” Phono-semantic matching from Coptic only attested by transcription in al-Maqrīzī as بلهيب and بلهويه which in turn is likely derived from Demotic Egyptian pꜣ-ḥwr (“Horon, a Canaanite god with whom the Sphinx was identi

By form a metathesis away from Coptic ⲉⲥⲑⲏⲙ (esthēm), though derivation from an unattested oblique δ (d) form of Ancient Greek στίμμι (stímmi) has been suggested, ultimately from Egyptian sdm, possibly also conflated with Egyptian msdmt.

parole.significato: Trifolium alexandrinum, Egyptian clover (a trefoil widely used as forage crop)
parole.testo: From Coptic ⲃⲉⲣⲥⲓⲙ (bersim, “Egyptian clover”), itself suggested a Middle Iranian borrowing, equalling Persian برسم (barsam, barsom) meaning a “bundle of twigs” of uncertain botanical identity brandished by Zoroastrians during recitation.

parole.significato: Pluchea (syn. subgenus Conyza subg. Leptogyne), especially Pluchea dioscoridis (syns. Conyza dioscoridis, Baccharis dio…
parole.testo: Derived from Coptic ⲃⲁⲣⲛⲁⲃⲓⲛ (barnabin), ⲃⲁⲣⲛⲟⲩⲃ (barnoub).
From Coptic *ⲡⲉⲧⲣⲱϣ (*petrōš, “the flamingo”), from Egyptian dšr. Also found metathesized as Tunisian Arabic شَبْرُوش (šabrūš, “flamingo”).

parole.significato: the roe of the flathead mullet (Mugil cephalus, بُورِيّ (būriyy)) and the sausage made thereof, bottarga
parole.testo: From Coptic ⲡⲓⲧⲁⲣⲓⲭⲓⲟⲛ (pitarikhion), from Ancient Greek τάριχος (tárikhos), which has also been borrowed directly as طِرِّيخ (ṭirrīḵ). The alternative forms come from reinterpreting the present form as a broken plural.
From Coptic ⲡⲉⲗϫⲱⲃ (peljōb), ⲡⲉⲗϭⲱⲃ (pelčōb).

parole.significato: mullet (several fish species, and especially Mugil cephalus)
parole.testo: * In Egypt, the name of the fish is said to come from Coptic ⲫⲟⲣⲓ (phori, “Mugil cephalus”) – in Bohairic, also ϥⲟⲣⲓ (fori), while in Sahidic it is ⲃⲱⲣⲉ (bōre); however, the name is also used in Morocco and Lebanon, and the relation with Japanese 鰡 / 鯔 (bora) denoting the same species of fish remain
Possibly from Coptic ⲙⲥⲁϩ (msah), from Egyptian G17-O34:V28-I3 mzḥ (“crocodile”) with the singular feminine definite article ⲧⲉ- (te-), though ⲙⲥⲁϩ (msah) is a masculine noun in Egyptian/Coptic.
From Coptic ϩⲁⲛϩⲧⲱⲱⲣ (hanhtōōr, literally “horses”).
Borrowed from Coptic ⲥⲓⲣ (sir).

Per Corriente, the term is borrowed from Coptic ⲥⲙⲟⲩⲛⲉ (smoune, “Nile goose”), only later shifting its meaning to that of سَلْوَى (salwā), for in the Classical Arabic dictionaries the present ornithonym is defined but vaguely.

parole.significato: Acacia spp. or Vachellia spp., especially Vachellia nilotica
parole.testo: Perhaps through Coptic ϣⲟⲛϯ (šonti), ultimately from Egyptian snḏt (/⁠ˈsantʼə/ < earlier /ˈsantʃʼat⁠/, “being feared, being respected, evoking reverence or respect; acacia”) stemming from its religious significance. Compare Akkadian 𒊭𒄠𒂅 (/⁠šamṭu, samṭu⁠/, “acacia”), a foreign loan suspected to be bo
From Coptic ϫⲉⲗϥⲁⲧ (jelfat), ⲥⲗⲃⲟⲧ (slbot). The form شِلْبَا (šilbā) appears most classical, compare also Ancient Greek σάλπη (sálpē), but in Egyptian Arabic the length is not pronounced.

parole.significato: an unknown kind of river fish, perhaps Petrocephalus bane
parole.testo: Apparently from Coptic ϣⲁⲗⲟⲩⲕⲓ (šalouki), ⲥⲁⲗⲟⲩⲕⲓ (salouki), from Egyptian šlq, alternative form of šrq, which also passed as شَرُّوك (šarrūk, “Schilbe”).

parole.significato: granary, any room for pitching corn
parole.testo: From Coptic, Sahidic Coptic ⲥⲏⲛⲉ (sēne), ⲥⲉⲛⲉ (sene), ⲥⲉⲛⲏ (senē), Bohairic Coptic ⲥⲏⲓⲛⲓ (sēini), ϣⲉⲩⲛⲉ (šeune, “heap, accumulation; granary”).
From the giant quarries of أُمّ الْصَوَّان (ʔumm al-ṣawwān) near أَسْوَان (ʔaswān), from Coptic ⲥⲟⲩⲁⲛ (souan), from Egyptian swnw s-wn:n-nw:W-T11:niwt
From Coptic ⲧⲱⲃⲉ (tōbe, “brick”), from Demotic Egyptian tb (“brick”), from Egyptian ḏbt (“brick, block, ingot”): Db-b-t:O39 potentially related to Sumerian 𒁾 (dub).

parole.significato: a brick, baked brick, adobe brick
parole.testo: From Coptic ⲧⲱⲃⲉ (tōbe, “brick”); see the etymology at طُوب (ṭūb).

parole.significato: the hook by which a bucket (قَادُوس (qādūs)) on a waterwheel is suspended
parole.testo: Through Coptic ⲡⲓⲕⲩⲣⲁⲝ (pikuraks) from Ancient Greek κόραξ (kórax).
Borrowed from Coptic ⲕⲁϣⲱ (kašō), from Egyptian qš.
Borrowed from Coptic ⲕⲣⲙⲉⲥ (krmes, “ash, soot”).

parole.significato: a kind of headdress consisting of a small cap environed by a gigantic turban, a bonnet, popular with the Ayyubids and M…
parole.testo: From Coptic ⲕⲗⲁϥⲧ (klaft, “calotte”) or/and from a feminine variant of Classical Syriac ܟܲܠܵܘܵܐ (kalāwā), ܟܲܠܘܵܐ (kalwā, “tiara”). See Latin calautica for more; possibly a doublet of قَلَنْسُوَة (qalansuwa).
Possibly borrowed from Coptic ⲕⲉⲛⲉⲫⲓⲧⲉⲛ (kenephiten) or from the root ك ن ف (k n f).

parole.significato: labeo (Labeo gen. et spp., especially Labeo niloticus)
parole.testo: From Coptic ⲗⲁⲃⲏⲥ (labēs).

parole.significato: vat, wide-bellied bowl, trough – such as for example a kneading trough, or a pottery coffin for burial until the IIIʳᵈ…
parole.testo: Generally believed to be of Coptic origin, however the exact word is omitted. One option is *ⲙⲁϫⲱⲣ (*majōr) from ⲙⲁ- (ma-, “place”) + ϫⲱⲣ (jōr, “to scatter”), another ⲙⲁⲕⲣⲟ (makro, “trough, mortar”) to which colloquial Egyptian Arabic could have applied the tool-pattern as in كَالُون (kālūn). Howeve

parole.significato: a coarse cloth, sackcloth, gunny, haircloth
parole.testo: This could be taken as from the root م س ح (m s ḥ) above as for a wiping rag, however the cloths denoted by this word do not seem to have been adapted for such an employment, and their property of coarseness makes the term adverse to that root’s meanings for smoothness. Borrowed from Coptic ⲟⲩⲁϩⲉ (ouahe).
From Coptic (Sahidic Coptic ⲟⲉⲓⲡⲉ (oeipe), Bohairic Coptic ⲱⲓⲡⲉ (ōipe)), from Egyptian jpt.
